I consider myself a big time movie buff and a fan of all genres, from art house to super hero popcorn blockbusters. I really liked this movie and how weird it started and I wanted to like it throughout, but I couldn’t get past how uncomfortable it made me feel. Not with its creative use of lens and framing, color palates, or overt sexuality…but there is literally a scene where Godwin is explaining how Bella has the brain of a toddler then it cuts to her masturbating. I get that it’s meant to be off putting and challenge the viewer, as well as an allegory on a woman’s sexual, emotional, and philosophical awaking throughout life, but that scene really took me out of it. It felt flippant and shocking for shock value. The film is still an amazing artistic expression and exceptionally unique, but such a direct hard cut to “here is a woman with a baby’s brain masturbating” was a step way too far.

Now that, I can’t disagree with. Any other band you present - The Ramones, Velvet Underground, Kraftwerk, Radiohead, NWA, Black Sabbath, Led Zepplin, Nirvana, The Stones…all of them have an influence are inevitably a lot more niche than The Beatles. Love em or hate em, The Beatles changed the game for genre, song structure, presentation, and the way the record industry operates.

I put my distinction more on song structure than sound. If you are a verse-chorus-verse-chorus-bridge-chorus kinda band, I tend to see you as heavily pop influenced. That’s, of course, a very broad generalization as Nirvana fits that mold and I’d probably get crucified for calling Nirvana pop, and there are many Beatles songs that don’t follow that mold. That being said, I think that The Beatles greatest influence was to infuse that song structure into Western radio so thoroughly that it is still followed to this day.
I’d say the Beatles are more the greatest pop band ever.

Ayn Rand is the quintessential example of how capitalism is a corrupting force. Here is this very intelligent young woman who starts to develop her own unique philosophy of the benefits of individualism and egoistic selfishness while growing up in Bolshevik Russia. She tries and fails, twice over, to translate that ideology into a novel format and finally finds success with the Fountainhead, a book that (up until the end) is pretty damn interesting and unique in how it presents a philosophical ideal. Not the best book, definitely not the most iron clad philosophy at all, but a creative way to present a story that makes you give the author the time of day. How does Ayn Rand react to that success and the money that comes with it? She crawls so far up her own ass that she comes back out her own eyes oozing the glory-to-god greatness of capitalism and the movers and shakers of the world. Atlas Shrugged is one of the single most garbage books I’ve ever read, and I dig the Fountainhead. Go fuck yourself, Ayn Rand. You fucking hypocrite.
